Furthermore, we investigated the impact of noise on model accuracy and identified that the architecture of the neural network plays a critical role in this context.

This paper investigates cyclic orbit codes within the vector space $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ and characterizes their associated code isometries. We demonstrate that every isometry of a cyclic orbit code is inherently a cyclic permutation acting on $\mathbb{F}_q^n$. Furthermore, we establish the condition under which the automorphism group of a cyclic orbit code consists solely of its cyclic permutations.

This paper investigates the spectral properties of the complex Schrödinger operator $\mathscr{L}_c=-d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$ defined on the half-line $[0,\infty)$, where the parameters satisfy $\alpha>0$ and $c\in\mathbb{C}$. We demonstrate that the system of eigenfunctions associated with $\mathscr{L}_c$ forms a complete set within the space $L^2([0,\infty))$.

This study introduces a refined Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method for simulating incompressible and compressible flows, grounded in a density-based framework. The approach employs a conservative formulation of the SPH equations, ensuring the preservation of mass, momentum, and energy. The incompressible constraint is enforced via a monolithic implicit pressure solver, while the density-based strategy facilitates the accurate computation of the equation of state and fluid property variations. The partition of unity and gradient approximation are enhanced by optimizing the smoothing length and the number of neighboring particles. The resulting algorithm is validated through various test cases, including incompressible free-surface flows, compressible shock waves, and multiphase interactions. The findings demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios involving shocks and complex free-surface dynamics.

Spectral super-resolution (SSR) is a critical task in hyperspectral imaging (HSI) that reconstructs high-resolution spectral data from low-resolution inputs. While deep learning has recently emerged as a promising solution for SSR, current methods often fail to account for the inherent sparsity of HSI spectral data. To address this, we introduce a novel deep neural network architecture designed to recover high-resolution spectra from their low-resolution counterparts. Our approach employs a function-mixture model to represent the spectral distribution, utilizing a pixel-aware mechanism to identify and isolate the most relevant spectral features. Furthermore, we incorporate a spectral sparsity loss function to enhance the accuracy of the recovered spectra. Extensive experiments conducted on two public datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This research introduces a geotagging framework that integrates contextual awareness to assign precise geotags to objects within images. The system employs a context-aware object detection model to identify and localize specific items in an image, followed by a geotagging module that determines their locations. This module incorporates contextual features to enhance the accuracy of these geotags. The study evaluates the proposed method using the MS-COCO dataset, where it demonstrates improved performance compared to existing state-of-the-art object geotagging approaches.

Remote sensing offers a valuable method for monitoring reservoirs, particularly in regions where ground-based data is scarce. However, the vast volume of imagery generated by these sensors makes it difficult to identify reservoirs manually. To address this, we introduce a tailored metric learning approach designed to locate dam reservoirs within remote sensing images. This method utilizes a deep learning framework to generate feature representations, which are then optimized using a metric learning loss function. This optimization ensures that features representing similar dam reservoirs are clustered closely together, while those representing dissimilar objects remain distant. We evaluated the proposed method using the Sentinel-2 satellite dataset and compared its performance against existing state-of-the-art techniques. The results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior accuracy compared to these baseline methods.

A QFS-space, defined as a quasi-F-space, serves as a generalization of the Tychonoff space concept by substituting the standard separation condition with the property of the quasi-separatedness of the space. This work examines the fundamental characteristics of QFS-spaces, including their relationship with the properties of P-spaces and the P-property, and explores how these spaces relate to the QFS framework. Furthermore, the study investigates the preservation of the QFS property under the formation of the product of two such spaces.

We introduce a method for pinpointing the type of a Point-of-Interest (POI) by analyzing user reviews. This approach leverages the rich semantic content within those reviews to forecast POI categories. To achieve this, we employ a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract features from review images and a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to derive features from review text. These extracted features are then integrated into a fully connected neural network to predict the specific POI type. To further enhance performance, we developed a hybrid model that combines our neural network with a traditional machine learning algorithm, utilizing a feature set that merges the neural network's output with additional hand-crafted features. Experimental results demonstrate that our hybrid model outperforms both the standalone neural network and the traditional machine learning model.

This study investigates the relationship between stock price movements and earnings calls. We analyzed transcripts from 1,000 randomly selected calls spanning 2010 to 2019, focusing on the temporal alignment between specific topics discussed and subsequent shifts in stock prices. Our findings indicate that the duration spent discussing topics related to financial performance, guidance, and acquisitions correlates with stock price changes within a 30-day window. Furthermore, we examined the sentiment of discussions regarding these key subjects and observed that a more negative tone in earnings call content is associated with subsequent declines in stock prices.

This study addresses the optimal deployment of sensors within homogeneous and heterogeneous wireless sensor networks (WSNs) characterized by restricted communication ranges. The primary objective is to maximize coverage efficiency by ensuring every point in the target area is monitored by at least $k$ sensors, where $k$ is a specified integer. The analysis begins with homogeneous WSNs, where all sensors share identical sensing radii. In this context, we derive the minimum number of sensors required for full coverage and establish the maximum achievable area. Furthermore, we examine heterogeneous WSNs, where sensors possess varying sensing radii. For these networks, we determine the minimum sensor count necessary to cover the entire target area. Additionally, we introduce a specific algorithm designed to arrange sensors of distinct sizes to achieve complete coverage.

This study introduces a quantum eigenstate filtering technique that leverages polynomial approximation to extract specific target eigenstates from the spectrum of a Hermitian matrix. The process involves two main steps: first, determining a polynomial that optimally filters these eigenstates; second, utilizing quantum signal processing to implement the derived polynomial. We demonstrate that this approach achieves a runtime complexity of $\mathcal{O}(1/\epsilon^2)$, where $\epsilon$ represents the desired accuracy. Furthermore, we apply this method to the quantum linear system problem, yielding an algorithm with a complexity of $\mathcal{O}(k^2 \log^2(1/\epsilon))$, where $k$ denotes the condition number of the matrix.

This study examines the existence of compact gauged baby skyrmions within a non-Abelian framework, specifically under conditions of self-duality. We demonstrate that these structures can be stabilized by embedding the gauged baby model into nonlinear dielectric media, where the stability is achieved through the confinement of the medium. Furthermore, we present numerical findings indicating that skyrmions with higher topological charges can be accommodated within the same spatial region when utilizing this self-dual compact model.

The Standard Model (SM) has been rigorously tested and validated through numerous experiments, yet it is not considered the final theory of particle physics. Numerous experiments have already placed stringent constraints on potential new physics, yet the SM remains incomplete. The Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) offers a systematic framework for investigating physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) by extending the SM Lagrangian with higher-dimensional operators. This work provides a comprehensive overview of current experimental efforts and future prospects in searching for BSM phenomena within the SMEFT framework.

A nuclear spin gyroscope is a device that determines orientation by measuring the precession of a spin around an external magnetic field. This precession frequency, which is proportional to the magnitude of the magnetic field, can be measured with exceptional precision. We introduce a new class of nuclear spin gyroscopes based on diamond, which utilizes the long-lived nuclear spin of $^{13}$C atoms. These gyroscopes are capable of detecting minute rotations with high accuracy and are distinguished by their immunity to magnetic field fluctuations, a property arising from the gyration occurring within the bulk material. Additionally, the device is compact, lightweight, and operates at room temperature.

Whole-cell computational models represent the most comprehensive quantitative depictions of cellular function, offering a holistic view of cellular behavior. These models are increasingly vital for advancing the field of synthetic biology, particularly in engineering complex systems that are difficult to predict using simplified approaches. This review examines the current state of the art in whole-cell modeling, covering both the underlying theoretical frameworks and the software tools employed. We also explore the key challenges associated with these models and outline the opportunities that lie ahead.

Mobile applications often require the capacity to capture objects from various angles, yet current research predominantly addresses single-view scenarios. This paper introduces a novel mobile multi-view object retrieval framework designed to handle such complex scenarios. The system operates in two distinct stages: first, it employs a multi-view object detector to identify objects across different perspectives, and second, it utilizes a multi-view image search algorithm to locate relevant images. We provide a comprehensive analysis of both the detection and retrieval components, evaluating their performance across diverse datasets. The study concludes with a practical demonstration of the complete framework within a mobile application.

This study introduces a hyperdimensional computing (HDC) framework designed for detecting epileptic seizures. The approach leverages the high-speed, high-accuracy, and energy-efficient characteristics of analog neuromorphic hardware, specifically Intel's Loihi, to execute the HDC algorithm. We evaluated the system using the CH-MIMIC dataset, which comprises electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings from 100 patients. The results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves a sensitivity of 99.9% and a specificity of 99.8%, confirming its effectiveness in seizure detection.

We investigate the potential of gravitational wave (GW) standard sirens to constrain the Hubble constant ($H_0$) using a forecast based on the Decihertz Observatory (DHO). We model the GW luminosity distance distribution as a function of redshift, treating the GW standard siren as a "dark siren" by assuming a uniform distribution of GW sources across the comoving volume. We demonstrate that the DHO can constrain the Hubble constant to a precision of 10% with 100 GW events, and 5% with 1,000 GW events. We also examine the impact of electromagnetic counterparts on this constraint, finding that while they improve the accuracy by 10% for 1,000 GW events, they offer no significant improvement for 100 GW events.

This paper introduces QALD-9+, a multilingual dataset designed for question answering that builds upon the original Question Answering over Linked Questions dataset (DBpedia) and Wikidata. This dataset is designed to support multilingual natural language processing tasks, including translation, cross-lingual question answering, and the creation of multi-lingual knowledge graphs. The dataset includes questions in 11 languages, each annotated with their corresponding answers from DBpedia and Wikidata resources. The dataset is available at https://multilingual-question-answering.github.io/.

This paper introduces Executive Function (EF), a contrastive value policy designed to enhance the resampling and relabeling of experiences within the agent's perceptual and value streams. By leveraging hindsight summarization, the model identifies and adjusts for biases in past experiences, thereby improving the accuracy of future predictions. The study demonstrates that applying this approach to the agent's perceptual and value streams leads to more accurate future predictions by correcting historical biases. Ultimately, this work establishes a framework for dynamically refining past experiences, which in turn enhances the reliability of future decision-making processes.

Bias in machine learning models can lead to unfair outcomes, yet identifying such bias in medical imaging remains challenging due to the scarcity of labeled data. This paper introduces a novel approach to detect bias in medical image datasets by leveraging the inherent structure of the data. We demonstrate that the primary challenge in this task is the lack of explicit labels, which we address by developing a new metric that quantifies the degree of bias. This metric is derived from the dataset's manifold structure, specifically by analyzing the relationship between the data and the learned representations. We further propose a novel unsupervised method to estimate bias levels using the properties of the data manifold. We evaluate this metric and the associated unsupervised technique on two publicly available medical imaging datasets, demonstrating their effectiveness in revealing hidden biases.

Metric learning aims to train models that generate similarity scores for data points, a task frequently applied in computer vision and natural language processing. While the Proxy-NCA loss has become a leading approach for this field, it is susceptible to noise caused by extreme positive and negative examples. This vulnerability can degrade model performance and hinder convergence. To address this, we introduce the Smooth Proxy-NCA loss, which mitigates noise by incorporating a smoothness constraint on the similarity scores. Our experiments demonstrate that this method achieves superior performance on various benchmarks, including face recognition, zero-shot learning, and retrieval tasks.

We introduce a novel statistical technique designed to extract cosmological parameters from galaxy surveys by analyzing the density-weighted pair separation function, $w(\theta, r|D)$. This metric represents the angular separation between galaxies, conditioned on their distance from the survey's density peak. By applying this method to the SDSS-III BOSS DR12 dataset, we derive constraints on the matter density parameter ($\Omega_{\rm m}$), the Hubble constant ($H_0$), and the amplitude of matter fluctuations ($\sigma_8$). Our results indicate that this approach yields constraints comparable in precision to those obtained using the traditional angular power spectrum.

We introduce an integrable model describing a topological SO(5) superfluid, which serves as a minimal integrable framework for a topological superfluid with SO(5) symmetry. This system is defined by a Hamiltonian featuring a topological term that breaks SO(5) symmetry down to SO(3) × SO(2). The model's integrability is established through the identification of an infinite set of conserved charges, which are derived from a Lax pair. We demonstrate that the model's integrability arises from a specific non-local transformation of the SO(5) symmetric Hamiltonian, which maps it into a form where the topological term is expressed as a bilinear combination of two SO(3) symmetric Hamiltonians.

This work introduces a novel, high-performance, large-area photodetector (MAPD) featuring a unique design that integrates the benefits of both avalanche photodiodes (APDs) and photodiodes (PDs). The device utilizes a specific doping profile to create a high-field region that triggers avalanche multiplication, while simultaneously maintaining a low-field region to facilitate carrier drift and minimize impact ionization. This architecture effectively balances the high gain of APDs with the superior noise performance of PDs. The study details the fabrication process, device structure, and resulting characteristics, including the analysis of the multiplication factor and its dependence on temperature. Additionally, the device's noise performance is evaluated, and a comparison is made with conventional PDs and APDs. The results indicate that the MAPD offers significantly lower noise than APDs while maintaining higher gain than PDs, making it an ideal choice for applications requiring both high sensitivity and low noise. The paper concludes with a discussion on the potential applications of the MAPD in fields such as optical communication, imaging, and sensing.

This paper examines the relationship between the sectional genera and local cohomology of graded Cohen-Macaulay rings, with a specific focus on graded Gorenstein rings. We demonstrate that local properties of the local ring at the origin of the ring can be inferred from its sectional genus function. Furthermore, we establish a connection between the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity and the sectional genera, proving that the ring's regularity is bounded above by a value dependent on the ring's dimension and the initial segment of the function. Finally, we derive an upper bound for the Hilbert series of graded Gorenstein rings, expressed in terms of the ring's dimension and its sectional genus sequence.

This study presents the first nuclear forward scattering (NFS) investigation of the high-pressure magnetic properties of the four-layered Aurivillius phase, $\text{Bi}_5\text{FeTi}_3\text{O}_{15}$. The research reveals a complex magnetic behavior characterized by a series of structural and electronic transitions. Specifically, the Fe$^{3+}$ ions undergo a spin reorientation transition at 1.2 GPa, while the $\text{Bi}^{3+}$ ions exhibit a spin reorientation transition at 1.5 GPa. Furthermore, the $\text{Bi}^{3+}$ ions display a pressure-induced valence transition at 1.5 GPa, and the $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions show a pressure-induced valence transition at 1.8 GPa. The magnetic dynamics of the $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions are described by a two-sublattice model, whereas the $\text{Bi}^{3+}$ ions are modeled using a three-sublattice framework. The study also identifies a pressure-induced structural transition occurring at 1.5 GPa, which is associated with a change in the crystallographic symmetry of the $\text{Bi}^{3+}$ ions.

This study introduces a Bayesian framework designed to rank brokers based on their execution algorithms. By modeling transaction costs as a Gaussian process, the approach estimates the relative performance of these systems. We demonstrate that this framework can be implemented using Gaussian processes and further illustrated through a case study involving real-world transaction cost data.

We introduce a proposal for fully reconfigurable optomechanical filters, specifically designed as add-drop cavities. This design utilizes a three-mode optomechanical cavity, where the middle mode is coupled to two distinct mechanical resonators. By adjusting the mechanical resonators' states, we can dynamically modify the filter's transmission spectrum, achieving both tunability and switching capabilities.

The internet has become a vital resource for disseminating information regarding public health, particularly during crises like the COVID-19 pandemic. This study examines the efficacy of public health interventions by analyzing how government websites and social media platforms communicate about COVID-19. We employed a novel, automated approach to quantify the textual content of these interventions, utilizing it to evaluate the alignment between official messaging and the public's information needs. Our results indicate that while government and health agency websites often prioritize their own institutional concerns, they frequently overlook the topics that are most relevant to the public.

This paper introduces a neural network designed for lossless image compression that has been thoroughly evaluated on the LBC-NR dataset. The architecture is built to be highly practical and efficient for implementation on GPUs, with an emphasis on optimizing the trade-off between compression ratio and computational cost. The proposed framework employs a streamlined, end-to-end design that utilizes a single encoder-decoder pair, integrating both a context model and a probability quantizer. The system is trained using a straightforward, end-to-end approach. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing neural approaches, while also outperforming the best conventional techniques by a significant margin.

The LHCb experiment has reported the first observation of the $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$ decay, with a significance exceeding $5.0\sigma$. This result is based on a data sample of $1.0\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ of proton-proton collisions collected at a center-of-mass energy of $7\,\text{TeV}$. The measured branching fraction is $(1.0\pm0.2\pm0.1)\times10^{-6}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic. Additionally, the analysis searches for the $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi$ decay, finding no evidence for it. The upper limit on its branching fraction is set at $<1.0\times10^{-6}$ at a $90\%$ confidence level.

Optimal transport (OT) has become a vital tool in machine learning, particularly for tasks like domain adaptation, where it estimates the mapping between a target distribution and a source distribution. However, the presence of outliers in the target data can severely compromise the performance of OT estimators. This paper introduces a novel, outlier-robust variant of OT designed to mitigate these effects. We demonstrate that our approach possesses robustness characteristics comparable to those of empirical risk minimization (ERM) in statistical learning. Specifically, the proposed method maintains stability even when the target distribution contains a significant number of outliers, provided the source distribution remains clean. Furthermore, the method is grounded in a Wasserstein barycenter framework, allowing it to handle multiple source distributions. We provide theoretical bounds on the impact of outliers on estimation error and validate our findings through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

Collaborative artificial intelligence (C-AI) represents a burgeoning field where humans and AIs function as a unified team. While existing research predominantly focuses on human-centric AI, this paper introduces a novel framework for developing collaborative agents capable of learning within human teams. We propose a hybrid reinforcement learning (RL) approach that integrates RL with human decision-making models to enable agents to learn collaboratively. This method employs a hybrid architecture combining RL with human models to generate a collaborative policy, which is subsequently optimized through RL. We validate this approach using a game-theoretic model of human behavior and a real-world negotiation benchmark. Results indicate that the hybrid method outperforms standard RL strategies, delivering more effective collaborative policies. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the hybrid approach can be extended to scenarios involving multiple AI teammates, successfully generating policies that enhance overall team performance.

This review examines the phenomenology of heavy supersymmetric particles, specifically focusing on pair production mechanisms at hadron colliders. It analyzes how these mechanisms are constrained by the mass of the lightest particle, the nature of the theory, and the energy scale of the experiment. Visualization tools are widely adopted across various fields to enhance data comprehension and decision-making. Although research has extensively examined how these tools impact performance and spatial reasoning, few studies have investigated differences across disciplines. This study addresses that gap by analyzing performance disparities among individuals from diverse professional backgrounds. We conducted a mixed-methods experiment involving 104 participants from four distinct fields: computer science, medicine, design, and journalism. Participants completed a spatial reasoning assessment using a 3D interactive visualization, followed by a survey assessing their attitudes toward the task. Results indicate that journalists and design students significantly outperformed other groups in both overall task success and spatial reasoning scores. Furthermore, exploratory analysis revealed that design students demonstrated superior performance in specific visualization tasks compared to other groups. These findings suggest that prior experience with data visualization and spatial reasoning are critical factors in success. Consequently, the study highlights the necessity of tailoring visualization research to account for the specific expertise of end-users.

This paper examines the relationship between induction and clause set cycles. We demonstrate that a clause set cycle can be derived from a set of clauses using only a limited form of induction. This result is further extended to show that induction is also applicable in broader contexts.

Graph retrieval involves identifying the most similar graphs from a database based on a query graph. This task is crucial for various applications, including chemical compound discovery, semantic web navigation, and social network analysis. This paper introduces a novel graph retrieval model designed to address this challenge. The proposed approach utilizes a matching model to evaluate the similarity between query and database graphs, employing a query-driven strategy to generate embeddings for database graphs. We assess the model's effectiveness across multiple graph datasets and compare its performance against existing state-of-the-art methods.

We introduce a novel framework for simulating transient dynamics in complex systems, drawing inspiration from the training methodologies used in natural language processing. This approach employs a recurrent neural network to forecast the subsequent state of a system based on its current configuration and a randomly selected set of other states. We evaluate this framework on a system of coupled oscillators, demonstrating that it successfully replicates the behavior of established models for synchrony and coherence.

This paper examines the application of fair division algorithms to electricity distribution, specifically addressing the challenge of allocating costs among customers. We introduce a straightforward and effective method for distributing expenses across a network of customers and distribution points, ensuring that the resulting cost allocation satisfies key fairness criteria.

Event coreference resolution (ECR) involves identifying links between event mentions within a document. This paper introduces a specialized ECR task designed for contentious political events, aiming to enhance the understanding of such occurrences. We present a dataset comprising 1,000 news documents covering ten specific contentious events, which were annotated by a team of three experts. We also developed a rule-based system to generate training data for fine-tuning a BERT model. Our results demonstrate that the model achieves state-of-the-art performance on this task.

This study introduces a novel class of valid inequalities for the complementarity knapsack problem (CKP), which is characterized by the constraint that for every pair of variables, their product must equal zero. The proposed inequalities are defined as convex, facet-defining over a substantial portion of the problem's feasible polytope, and capable of being computed in polynomial time. Additionally, we present a method for separating these inequalities in polynomial time. Finally, we integrate these inequalities into a branch-and-cut-and-lift framework designed for solving CKPs.

In this paper, we investigate generalized $(m, n)$-derivations and centralizers within the context of $m$-torsion free, semiprime rings. Furthermore, we establish findings concerning the nature of generalized $(m, n)$-derivations when their associated left ideals are assumed to be two-sided.

We demonstrate that the two-component formalism can be derived from the 2-factor of the 4-component Dirac spinor, a result that is valid for any helicity value. Furthermore, a 4-component spinor is established to be the direct product of a 2-component spinor and a 2-spinor carrying helicity $\pm \frac{1}{2}$. This equivalence is demonstrated to be true for particles with mass as well.

We define a transversal family as a collection of sets where any two members intersect in a set of zero measure. This concept extends the notion of a transversal family, a property known as being a "thick family" when the sets have positive Hausdorff dimension. We establish a sufficient condition for a family of projections to form a transversal family, thereby extending a result by Bourgain and Guth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a thick family of projections constitutes a transversal family provided the projections are not concentrated on a specific submanifold. This finding broadens a result by Wolff and provides a novel characterization of sets possessing positive or infinite generalizations of one-dimensional and higher-dimensional Favard lengths.

This paper introduces a data-efficient algorithm for solving continuous control tasks, which combines the stability guarantees of Lyapunov-based MPC with Guided Policy Search (GPS). The method employs MPC to construct a tube around a reference trajectory, ensuring the closed-loop system maintains stability and then uses GPS to optimize the trajectory and tube parameters by imitating the MPC outputs. This approach is demonstrated on a challenging contact-rich task involving a quadruped robot balancing on a moving surface. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms both standard MPC and standard GPS in terms of sample efficiency and final task performance.

The third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (IAHE) is a recently identified transport phenomenon occurring in non-magnetic materials lacking inversion symmetry. This effect arises from the Berry curvature gradient, which is the spatial derivative of the Berry curvature. In this study, we establish a generalized semiclassical framework for the IAHE that incorporates the influence of external electric and magnetic fields. We demonstrate that this generalized IAHE exhibits a linear dependence on the magnetic field, a property that distinguishes it from the original IAHE. Furthermore, we investigate the IAHE within the context of the Weyl semimetal, where we find that the IAHE can be expressed as a summation of two distinct components: one stemming from the Berry curvature gradient and the other from the magnetic monopole charge.

Call graphs serve as a vital instrument for comprehending the internal workings of software systems. While numerous studies have developed methods to automatically generate call graphs, comparatively few have examined how to visualize multiple such graphs. This paper introduces an approach to the scalable visual comparison of an ensembled call graphs, designed to facilitate the identification of both common and distinct patterns. We present a novel, scalable technique for graph layout that enables the simultaneous rendering of many call graphs, allowing users to interactively adjust the number of displayed instances. This interactivity supports the detection of recurring patterns, while also offering a mechanism to isolate unique occurrences. We validated our approach through a case study involving the comparison of call graphs derived from 1,000 Java programs.

The One Billion Word Benchmark (OWB) is a widely used dataset for evaluating language modeling, yet it is constructed from a single news archive covering only 13 years. This narrow scope creates a significant issue: the resulting language models are heavily biased toward news content, which distorts their ability to perform various natural language processing tasks. This paper investigates the extent of this bias and proposes a solution to mitigate it. We demonstrate that the bias is substantial and that the bias can be effectively reduced by training models on corpora containing a higher proportion of non-news text.

Quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) are a common feature of solar flares, yet their physical origins remain unclear. This study investigates the relationship between QPPs and the dynamics of the flare current sheet (CS) by analyzing microwave emissions from a specific solar flare. We utilized the Nobeyama Radioheliograph (NHR) to observe microwave radiation at 17 GHz and the Nobeyama 45-m telescope at 17.2 GHz to capture the spatial distribution of these emissions. Our analysis reveals that the 17 GHz radio flux exhibits a QPP with a period of approximately 100 seconds, while the 17.2 GHz data shows a spatially localized QPP occurring within the flare's microwave bright region. Furthermore, the 17.2 GHz QPPs display a period of roughly 10 seconds, which aligns with the oscillation timescale of the flare CS. We propose that the 17 GHz QPPs arise from the electron beam's interaction with the expanding current sheet, whereas the 17.2 GHz QPPs are generated by the electron beam's interaction with the oscillating current sheet itself.

This paper introduces a multi-scale anomaly detection method designed for industrial quality inspection, utilizing a Contrario framework. The approach employs a multi-scale strategy to capture anomalies across various dimensions, including those that are both localized and extensive. The method's effectiveness is validated through a case study focused on detecting defects in printed circuit board (PCB) assembly.

Kramers' theorem guarantees that the energy levels of a spin-1/2 system with time-reversal symmetry are always degenerate. This work investigates how this degeneracy persists in the presence of dissipation, specifically within a two-level open quantum system coupled to a bosonic bath. We demonstrate that while degeneracy is generally broken, the energy levels can become degenerate again under specific conditions. This paper examines the nature of this "revival" of degeneracy and analyzes the factors that determine whether it occurs.

This study introduces a machine learning-based framework for downlink channel state information (CSI) prediction in high-mobility massive MIMO environments. The proposed method utilizes a deep neural network (DNN) to forecast future CSI, enabling the base station to determine optimal precoding matrices for subsequent time slots. By leveraging this prediction capability, the system can maintain effective downlink transmission even when users move rapidly and existing CSI becomes outdated. Simulation results demonstrate that the approach significantly enhances downlink throughput in highly mobile scenarios.

This study introduces a Bayesian hierarchical model designed to estimate inequality metrics across small geographic areas. The approach leverages a mixture of Beta distributions to define the data's likelihood, offering greater flexibility than standard parametric models. The resulting framework is applied to assess income and wealth disparities within the United Kingdom.

This work examines the Szeg\H{o} kernel associated with the boundary of the holomorphic Bergman kernel space associated to a complex Riemannian manifold, utilizing Grauert tube techniques. We derive an expansion for the kernel valid in the limit as the tube radius approaches zero, with coefficients expressed through local geometric data. This expansion serves as a refined generalization of established results for step functions on compact groups and Sasakian manifolds. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the diagonal of this kernel exhibits a complete asymptotic expansion as the tube radius shrinks, with coefficients determined by intrinsic geometric invariants of the manifold.

This paper presents MARINLINGA, a novel algorithm for constructing reverse line graphs (RLGs) of simple graphs. It addresses the limitations of the previously best-known method, Roussopoulos's algorithm, which relies on the complement graph and often encounters performance bottlenecks with dense inputs. By utilizing the graph's adjacency matrix, the MARINLINGA algorithm is designed to be more efficient when processing dense graphs. Additionally, the study introduces a new class of graphs termed MARINLINGA-irreducible, which are precisely those cases where the algorithm's performance is suboptimal. Finally, the authors provide a formal proof of the algorithm's correctness.
The article provides a verification of Lee-Lee's conjecture, which addresses the geometric properties of rigid modules within the upper triangular $n \times n$ quiver.

Java developers frequently encounter the challenge of managing excessive dependencies, which can lead to bloated applications. This study examines the evolution of Java dependency usage over time, specifically focusing on how their quantity and size change. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of 1,000 Java projects from the GitHub repository, tracking how dependency counts and sizes fluctuate longitudinally. Our results indicate that while dependency counts often decrease over time, their size tends to grow. Furthermore, we observed that approximately 60% of all dependencies are marked for removal at some point, with about 40% of all dependencies being newly added. We also discovered that the removal of dependencies is primarily driven by updates to the project's own dependencies. Finally, we provide practical recommendations for developers to effectively manage and reduce dependency bloat.

We demonstrate that the kinship and antagonism of quantum chains play a crucial role in the entangled biphoton-controlled synthesis of quantum states. This phenomenon is characterized by the entangled biphoton's ability to probabilistically steer the quantum state of a target chain. This steering effect is achieved by manipulating the quantum correlations between the biphoton and a control qubit. Our findings indicate that the probability of successfully synthesizing a specific quantum state within the target chain can be adjusted by modulating the quantum correlations linking the biphoton and the control qubit. This approach offers a new method for probabilistic quantum state engineering in quantum information processing.

This study examines multistage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) problems characterized by nested uncertainty sets, which are prevalent in practical applications. We introduce a novel multistage DRO framework that accommodates any distribution within a specified family, provided it shares the same support as a reference distribution. This approach is versatile enough to handle various distance metrics, including total variation (TV) and Wasserstein distances. We demonstrate that the optimal value of the resulting robust optimization problem can be expressed as a value-at-risk (VaR) of the cost function relative to the reference distribution. Furthermore, we establish that the optimal recourse policy is uniquely determined by this optimal value. We also prove that the optimal robust value remains invariant across different choices of base distributions, a finding that validates the concept of "effective scenarios." These results indicate that the robust optimization problem is effectively static, as it relies solely on the reference distribution rather than the full uncertainty set. We further show that the optimal robust value is a function of the reference distribution's VaR at a specific confidence level, which is determined by the uncertainty set and the cost function. Consequently, the robust optimization problem can be solved efficiently by first computing the VaR of the cost function with respect to the reference distribution and then applying the corresponding VaR-based policy. This approach offers a significant computational advantage over traditional multistage DRO methods, which typically require solving complex optimization problems at each stage.

This study introduces a new deep learning framework designed to anticipate human actions by integrating a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). The CNN extracts features from input images, which are subsequently mapped into a high-dimensional latent space via a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel. This transformation enhances the RNN's ability to capture complex, high-dimensional temporal patterns. The RBF kernel is employed to create a nonlinear mapping that preserves the topological relationships of the data. To address the challenge of limited training data, the model leverages the generalization capabilities of the RBF kernel. Furthermore, the RBF kernel is optimized using a gradient-based approach, and the entire system is trained end-to-end. Experimental results demonstrate that this architecture outperforms existing methods in predicting human actions.

We introduce a solvable model for a quantum many-body system that undergoes thermalization to a distinct, non-equilibrium steady state (NESS) after unitary evolution. This system comprises a central region of interacting fermions connected to two leads, which are individually driven by periodic Hamiltonians. While these drives operate at the same frequency, they possess different phases, resulting in two separate drive periods—a scenario mimicking the design of a quantum device with components operating at disparate clock speeds. We demonstrate that the resulting NES possesses a non-trivial spectral structure, characterized by a non-zero spectral gap and a non-vanishing density of states. Furthermore, we find that the NES can be described by a thermal distribution with a non-uniform temperature profile, where temperature varies as a function of position.

This study establishes the necessary and sufficient conditions for a pseudo-differential operator on a homogeneous tree to exhibit boundedness and compactness within the Hardy space $H^1$, as well as in the space of vanishingly continuous and rapidly decreasing functions at infinity. Furthermore, the authors derive sufficiency criteria regarding the symbols that guarantee pseudo-differential operators are nuclear operators acting between the specified function spaces.

The fifth generation (5G) of mobile networks is designed to deliver significantly higher data rates, lower latency, and enhanced reliability compared to previous generations. This advancement is achieved through the use of millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequencies, which offer wider bandwidths but suffer from limited propagation distances and high susceptibility to blockage. Consequently, mmWave signals are predominantly confined to the immediate vicinity of base stations, known as hotspots. This study examines the spatial distribution of 5G coverage within urban environments, utilizing a dataset of 1.2 million GPS points collected from 5G-capable smartphones across 100 distinct areas in the city of Rome. The findings reveal that 5G connectivity is highly localized, with hotspot coverage extending only 100 to 200 meters from the base station. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the coverage footprint of 5G hotspots is primarily determined by the specific mmWave frequency band employed.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success across various domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. However, these models often exhibit overconfidence when encountering out-of-distribution (OOD) data, a tendency that can lead to severe consequences in critical sectors like healthcare and autonomous driving. To address this, we introduce a novel, model-agnostic method for identifying OOD samples by leveraging the inherent characteristics of neural networks. Our approach, named **CODE** (Chamfer Out-of-Distribution Examples), utilizes the **Chamfer Distance** metric to measure the discrepancy between the feature representations of input data and the model's learned representations. We demonstrate that this metric effectively captures the structural differences between in-distribution and out-of-distribution samples. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse neural network architectures validate the method's efficacy. Furthermore, we show that the proposed approach can be seamlessly integrated with existing OOD detection techniques to enhance their performance.

This study presents the first azimuthal correlations for inclusive 2-jet, 3-jet, and 4-jet events in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, utilizing the CMS detector at the LHC. The analysis focuses on the differential cross sections for the dijet, trijet, and 4-jet systems as a function of the azimuthal angle difference between the leading jets. The observed data are compared against predictions from the PYTHIA 8, HERWIG++ 2.9, and SHERPA 2.0 Monte Carlo event generators. The results indicate that PYTHIA 8 and SHERPA 2.0 provide a superior description of the dijet azimuthal correlations compared to HERWIG++ 2.9. Furthermore, the measured 3-jet and 4-jet differential cross sections are consistent with PYTHIA 8 and SHERPA 2.0 predictions, whereas HERWIG++ 2.9 exhibits a significant discrepancy with the data.

Deep learning has achieved significant success across numerous computer vision tasks, including image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation. However, the majority of these algorithms depend on large volumes of labeled data, which are often costly and time-consuming to acquire. To address this, researchers have developed various semi-supervised and unsupervised deep learning approaches that utilize unlabeled data to enhance model performance. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of these techniques, covering both semi-supervised and unsupervised deep learning methods. It begins by examining the application of unsupervised deep learning in image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation. Subsequently, it reviews the use of semi-supervised deep learning in these same tasks. Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion on future research directions and unresolved challenges within the fields of unsupervised and semi-supervised deep learning.

Outlier detection is a critical task in data mining, yet most existing methods struggle with high-dimensional data. This paper introduces RECol, a straightforward yet effective approach that generates reconstruction error columns by measuring the discrepancy between original data points and their approximations derived from a low-rank matrix factorization. By utilizing these reconstruction error columns, RECol transforms the detection challenge into a standard classification problem. The method is evaluated on various real-world datasets, demonstrating its superior performance compared to other algorithms.

This study examines a broad category of non-linear equations driven by the rough path $\mathbf{y}=(y,\mathbf{z})$ within the framework of rough differential equations. We demonstrate that if $\mathbf{y}$ possesses $\alpha$-Hölder continuity with $\alpha > 1/\gamma$ (where $\gamma > 1$ is the Hölder exponent of the driver $y$), then the solution $x$ exhibits $\lfloor \alpha\gamma \rfloor$-regularity in the same $\alpha$-Hölder metric. Furthermore, we establish an alternative sufficient condition: when $\mathbf{y}$ is $\lfloor \alpha\gamma \rfloor$-regular with $\alpha > 1/\gamma$, the resulting solution $x$ becomes $\lfloor \alpha\gamma \rfloor$-regular. These findings are applied to establish the $\lfloor \alpha\gamma \rfloor$-regularity of the solution $u$ to the parabolic rough PDE $du_t = A u_t dt + \mathbf{f}dx_t$ on a bounded domain, subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. Here, $\mathbf{f}dx_t$ represents a stochastic term linked to the rough path $\mathbf{y}$, and the operator $A$ is an elliptic operator of order $2\gamma$.

We investigate the polarizability of neutrinos within a framework of non-minimal flavor interactions, where neutrinos couple to a scalar field via a non-minimal term. This interaction induces neutrino pair production in strong electromagnetic fields, a process we analyze using a Schwinger-Dalembert equation for the fermion propagator. Our findings demonstrate that the pair production rate increases significantly with higher coupling constants. Additionally, we examine the impact of this polarizability on neutrino propagation through matter, revealing that the resulting effective potential can be substantially larger than the standard MSW potential.

This study examines the dynamics of a neuronal-glial network modeled as a mean field system, where neurons and glial cells are represented by two coupled oscillators. The interaction between these oscillators is governed by a non-linear coupling function that incorporates a Hill function, reflecting the biochemical exchange of ATP and adenosine triphosphate (ATP). The research investigates how varying coupling strengths and Hill coefficients influence the system's dynamic behavior. Findings indicate that the model can reproduce both spontaneous oscillations and synchronization phenomena observed in biological systems. Furthermore, the model demonstrates bistability, where the system can exist in either a synchronized or non-synchronized state depending on initial conditions. The authors also explore the impact of external stimuli on the system's behavior, revealing that the response is contingent upon the initial state. The results suggest that the model can effectively capture the complex dynamics of the neuron-glial network, including the emergence of novel oscillatory patterns. The study concludes that the model provides a valuable framework for understanding the functional roles of glial cells in regulating neuronal activity.

This study examines the Berry phase acquired by a neutral spin-1/2 particle subjected to a magnetic field, focusing on its topological characteristics. We demonstrate that by manipulating the particle's trajectory and its internal degrees of freedom, the resulting Berry phase can be either $\pi$ or 0. We further analyze the geometric attributes of this phase, including its topological charge and the associated gauge potential and curvature. We also discuss the physical ramifications of these findings for both abelian and non-abelian contexts.

The study examines a one-dimensional random walk confined within a moving boundary that retreats at a constant velocity, where retreat is triggered by the arrival of a "first-passage" event. This event occurs when the walker crosses a specific threshold, causing the threshold itself to shift backward by a fixed amount. This dynamic framework models the degradation of a material's surface under cyclic loading, where the threshold represents a surface flaw that expands with each stress cycle once a fatigue event is triggered. We analyze the statistical properties of the system, specifically the probability of the walker reaching a critical point before the boundary retreats beyond a safe limit, as well as the long-term distribution of the boundary's position. We also identify a critical transition in the system's behavior: when the boundary's retreat speed exceeds a specific rate, the probability of failure drops to zero, indicating that failure becomes impossible.

This paper examines the relationship between hyperbolic L-space knots and their formal semigroups, which are derived from the counts of instanton Floer homology. We present evidence supporting the conjecture that this class of L-space knots is confined to the family of torus knots. Specifically, we demonstrate that any L-space knot $K$ with genus $g(K) \geq 2$ satisfying $|K| \leq 2$ must be a torus knot. Furthermore, we establish that for a hyperbolic L-space knot $K$ with $g(K) \geq 3$, the inequality $|K| \geq 3$ holds.

We present a Poisson bracket structure for the space of specific entropy-functional-dependent variables linked to kinetic theory, alongside a corresponding bracket in phase space for entropy-conserving dynamics. We establish a Poisson bracket morphism mapping entropy-functional-dependent variables in this kinetic theory space to a phase space for entropy-conserving dynamics. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this mapping aligns the Poisson bracket structure of the kinetic functional dependency space with the bracket structure in entropy-conserving phase space. We also show that the Poisson bracket structure in the kinetic functional dependency space is compatible with the bracket structure in entropy-conserving phase space. This study introduces a novel ensemble methodology designed to enhance the robustness of object detection within endoscopic video streams. The approach leverages a diverse collection of state-of-the-art detectors, including YOLOv4, YOLOv5, and Faster R-CNN, to establish a baseline ensemble. To further enhance this system, we developed a new algorithm for selecting the optimal set of detectors based on specific video characteristics. Additionally, we proposed a technique to mitigate false positives by filtering out detections that persist for only brief intervals. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed ensemble framework achieves superior performance compared to individual detectors and the initial baseline ensemble.

Identifiers are fundamental to programming languages, serving as the primary mechanism for naming variables, functions, and classes. While developers often rely on these identifiers to convey semantic meaning, they frequently violate coding standards, leading to confusion and reduced code readability. This paper examines the structural and semantic characteristics of identifiers within C and C++ projects. We introduce a novel methodology for automatically detecting grammar patterns in identifiers, which are subsequently analyzed to reveal the structural and semantic organization of names. Our findings indicate that these patterns are prevalent across both languages, though they exhibit distinct differences in how they are utilized. Furthermore, we demonstrate that grammar patterns can effectively represent the semantics of identifiers, with specific patterns correlating to particular naming conventions.

We demonstrate that the Fock space associated with a quantum shuffle algebra for affine $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2$ constitutes an irreducible highest weight module of the affine Lie algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2$, characterized by marks $(1,1)$ and a formal parameter $q$. This construction parallels the well-known Fock space for the affine Lie algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_1$. Furthermore, we prove that the Fock space for a quantum shuffle algebra of affine Lie algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_n$ is equivalent to the quantum vertex Weyl module $\square_q(\Lambda_0)$, a result that extends and confirms a previously established theorem by K. Prikhod'ko.

This study introduces a novel data-driven approach for analyzing grain growth in duplex and triplex microstructures. By employing a data-driven methodology, we extract grain-growth kinetics from a vast number of grains, enabling the identification of distinct growth behaviors across various grain size populations. This technique is demonstrated using a phase-field model of grain growth in duplex systems, where the grain-growth kinetics are defined by a single parameter, $P$, representing the grain-growth mobility. We subsequently extend this framework to triplex systems, where the kinetics are governed by three distinct mobility parameters. This triplex model is validated against experimental data from a triplex microstructure, confirming the approach's effectiveness.

This study introduces a benchmark for evaluating 3D human pose and shape estimation, derived from the NYU-R1 dataset. The paper details the dataset's construction, including the collection of 3D scans and ground-truth annotations, as well as the methodology for generating training and testing splits. We also present a comprehensive analysis of the estimation task, covering the influence of ground-truth noise, the impact of initial pose estimates, and the relationship between pose and shape. The work concludes with a baseline implementation of a deep learning model for 3D pose and shape prediction, which serves as a reference point for future research.

We investigate the BCS pairing mechanism within a dilute system of non-interacting Fermi gases, where attractive forces between electrons are localized at specific sites. This study examines the relationship between the critical temperature ($T_c$) and the concentration of attractive sites, as well as the behavior of $T_c$ in the limit of strong binding energy. Our analysis reveals that for sufficiently strong binding, the system undergoes a transition from a BCS regime to a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) type of superconductivity.

We introduce a model-independent framework for computing Wilson coefficients of effective operators that couple scalar leptoquarks to Standard Model quarks and leptons. This approach utilizes a single effective Lagrangian that accurately describes the lepton and quark interactions of a scalar leptoquark across diverse kinematic regimes, from the effective field theory limit to the regime where individual particle masses are significant. By integrating this model-independent formalism with specific theoretical models, we demonstrate its efficacy in deriving Wilson coefficients for various scenarios.

Machine learning has become a cornerstone of modern artificial intelligence, with deep learning serving as its most prominent and successful application. This paper explores the utility of category theory as a framework for modeling deep learning systems. By leveraging the abstraction capabilities inherent in category theory, we can formulate deep learning architectures within a more generalized mathematical context. This formalization facilitates a deeper comprehension of these systems and lays the groundwork for investigating their fundamental properties.

This study introduces a novel optimal terminal sliding-mode control (OTSMC) method designed to achieve finite-time convergence in second-order motion systems. By employing a newly designed optimal sliding surface, the proposed approach ensures that the system state reaches the desired target in a pre-specified time while maintaining a specific convergence rate. The robustness of the OTSMC is demonstrated through a Lyapunov-based proof. Furthermore, the absence of chattering is addressed by implementing a terminal attractor mechanism. To validate the method's efficacy, a numerical simulation is conducted on a robotic manipulator, with results compared against existing finite-time control strategies.

Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are essential for modern energy storage and electric mobility, yet their internal architecture remains largely inaccessible to direct observation. This study introduces a non-destructive ultrasonic technique capable of characterizing the layered structure within LIBs. By utilizing a custom-built ultrasonic resonator, we measured the resonance frequencies of various electrode materials and correlated these values with the speed of sound in each substance. This approach enables the calculation of the thickness of individual layers in a stacked electrode assembly. Furthermore, we demonstrated the method's utility by analyzing a commercial cell, successfully estimating the thickness of its components with an accuracy of approximately 10%.

This paper introduces a discrete-time flatness-based control framework designed for gantry cranes. The methodology involves deriving a discrete flatness model by applying a zero-order hold to the continuous flatness-based dynamics of the system. The efficacy of the proposed control approach is validated through numerical simulations.

Image captioning involves generating textual descriptions for images, a task that typically relies on large-scale datasets. However, these datasets often contain noisy labels, which can degrade the performance of models trained on them. This paper introduces a cooperative distillation approach to mitigate the impact of noisy labels in image captioning. The method employs a dual-teacher architecture consisting of a visual teacher and a linguistic teacher. The visual teacher analyzes image content to produce accurate visual descriptions, while the linguistic teacher ensures grammatical correctness and proper word usage. By combining these complementary signals, the system generates high-quality pseudo-labels that effectively guide the training of a student model. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art solutions on the MS-COCO benchmark.

A collection of strings is defined as well-connected if it can be constructed by starting with a single string and repeatedly appending strings that share at least $|S|-1$ consecutive characters with the current union. We demonstrate that determining whether a given set qualifies as well-connected is NP-complete. Additionally, we establish a lower bound of $\Omega(n^2)$ for the time required to verify well-connectedness, while also presenting an algorithm with $O(n^2)$ runtime to solve this problem.

Ehresmann semigroups are defined as semigroups that are simultaneously semilactes and right regular semigroups. This paper establishes the theory of ordered Ehresmann semigroups by extending the concept of ordered semigroups to these structures, specifically by defining a compatible ordering based on the partial orders found in the constituent right regular semigroup and the inverse semilattice. Furthermore, we establish a connection between ordered Ehresmann semigroups and ordered categories through the use of morphisms, providing an explicit definition of the ordering within these categories.

Self-attention mechanisms have become a cornerstone of modern deep learning, driving significant advancements across various domains. While these models are typically trained using standard techniques like stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and often optimized by adjusting hyperparameters such as layer count and width, the specific impact of depth (the number of layers) remains poorly understood. This study investigates the interaction between depth and width in self-attention architectures. We demonstrate that the interplay between these factors is critical for model performance. Specifically, we identify that the depth-to-width ratio is a key determinant of the optimal architecture, with the ideal configuration varying based on the dataset. Furthermore, we propose a novel method to estimate the appropriate depth-to-width ratio for a given task. Empirical results indicate that this approach effectively predicts optimal architectures, thereby reducing the need for extensive hyperparameter tuning.

This study details the synthesis of BiFeO$_{3}$ nanoparticles (NPs) via a sol-gel method at low temperatures, followed by characterization using XRD, FE-SEM, and TEM. The resulting nanoparticles exhibit a hexagonal morphology with a particle size of approximately 10 nm. Analysis of the magnetic properties at room temperature reveals a saturation magnetization of 1.2 emu/g, which is significantly higher than that of bulk BiFeO$_{3}$, attributed to the material's nanoscale dimensions. Furthermore, the sample demonstrates excellent photo-ferroelectric behavior under illumination. The photocatalytic efficiency of these BiFeO$_{3}$ NPs was evaluated through the degradation of Methylene Blue dye and the production of hydrogen gas. The results indicate that the material is highly effective for both applications, suggesting that BiFeO$_{3}$ NPs are a promising candidate for solar water splitting.

We examine a toy model featuring a unified gauge group of ${\rm SU}(6)$, which breaks down to ${\rm SU}(3)_C \times {\rm SU}(3)_L \times {\rm SU}(3)_R$. This framework accommodates three generations of fermions, each residing within a ${\bf 6}$ representation of the parent ${\rm SU}(6)$ group. The Yukawa interactions are defined by a Yukawa matrix that transforms as a ${\bf 35}$ under ${\rm SU}(6)$. The model's Higgs sector includes a ${\bf 35}$ scalar and a ${\bf 64}$ scalar, both of which acquire vacuum expectation values. The ${\bf 35}$ scalar is responsible for generating masses for the bottom quark and the tau lepton, while the ${\bf 64}$ scalar generates masses for the top quark and the W and Z bosons. Theoretical predictions for the masses of the bottom quark and tau lepton align well with observed experimental values.

This study introduces a novel 3D hand-object reconstruction challenge focused on generic objects, which are typically encountered in daily life. We present the GeneralObjectHands (GOH) dataset, comprising 10,000 images of hands interacting with such items. This collection includes 100 distinct hand-object categories, featuring 100 instances of each class. To address the scarcity of labeled data, we developed a semi-supervised learning approach that leverages unlabeled images alongside a small set of labeled examples. This method utilizes a combination of self-supervised learning and contrastive learning to extract meaningful features from the unlabeled data. We further validate the effectiveness of this technique by applying it to the GOH dataset. Our experimental results demonstrate that this semi-supervised learning approach significantly outperforms fully supervised learning methods, achieving a 10% improvement in performance.

The Ca II K-line serves as a primary indicator of solar chromospheric activity, with its variability linked to numerous solar phenomena. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the Ca II K index and spectral line profiles spanning 1917 to 2017, utilizing a dataset of 104 years of equal-contrast images from the Kodaikanal Observatory. This extended time frame allows for the examination of solar activity cycles and long-term trends. Our findings reveal that the Ca II K index exhibits a significant correlation with the Wolf sunspot number, with a correlation coefficient of 0.73. Furthermore, we identified a notable decline in the Ca II K index during the declining phase of solar cycles 19 and 20, a trend that aligns with observations from the National Solar Observatory (NSO). Additionally, we observed a decrease in the equivalent width of the Ca II K line during the declining phase of solar cycle 20. Finally, we detected a significant correlation between the Ca II K index and the Wolf sunspot number during the rising phase of solar cycles 19 and 20, with a correlation coefficient of 0.74.

The study presents the first observation of the $\Sigma^+ \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$ decay, with a measured branching fraction of $(1.16 \pm 0.20 \text{ (stat)} \pm 0.12 \text{ (syst)}) \times 10^{-10}$ based on $pp$ collision data collected by the LHCb experiment at center-of-mass energies of 7, 8, and 13 TeV, totaling an integrated luminosity of 9 fb$^{-1}$. This result represents a significant improvement over the previous world-leading limit, which was approximately an order of magnitude lower. Furthermore, the analysis examines the angular distribution of the final state, the decay's CP asymmetry, and the potential for new physics, concluding that no significant deviations from the Standard Model are observed.

Symbolic execution is a widely used technique for uncovering software bugs, yet scaling it to large-scale systems remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a new distributed symbolic execution framework designed to address this issue. We propose a novel partitioning strategy based on test depth, which ensures that the execution paths of a given program are distributed across different workers in an efficient and balanced manner. We have implemented this strategy within a new framework called DSE-TP and evaluated it against two existing tools, showing that our approach outperforms them in both parallel execution speed and the number of execution paths discovered.

We investigate the relaxation dynamics of magnetization in chains of magnetic nanoparticles, where interparticle interactions are modeled using the classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian. By applying the linear response theory, we derive the dynamic susceptibility and identify a relaxation spectrum characterized by a distribution of rates. Our analysis reveals that the susceptibility's dependence on temperature and frequency is governed by the distribution of activation energies and attempt frequencies. Furthermore, we examine the impact of randomizing particle orientations on these relaxation parameters and demonstrate that the susceptibility can be effectively described using a two-parameter distribution.

Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning framework designed to train models across multiple devices without transmitting raw data to a central server. While traditional FL relies on a central server, this approach often incurs significant communication costs and raises privacy concerns. To address these issues, social network-based FL (SNL-FL) has emerged, leveraging existing social structures to facilitate decentralized training. This paper introduces a novel, decentralized FL model specifically for single-sided trust social networks. We propose a distributed algorithm that enables participants to collaboratively train a global model without a central coordinator. By utilizing a social graph, the algorithm distributes the training process across multiple layers, allowing each participant to refine the global model through local updates and exchanges with trusted neighbors. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to traditional FL systems while significantly reducing communication overhead.

This study introduces a sequential short-text classification framework that leverages the inherent order of text sequences. By integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), the model utilizes CNNs to extract features from individual short texts and applies RNNs to capture the sequential dependencies between consecutive texts. Evaluated on benchmark datasets for emotion detection and spam identification, our approach outperforms standalone RNN and CNN architectures. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that incorporating sequential information yields superior performance compared to relying solely on isolated texts.

Fabry-P\'erot (FP) etalons are fundamental instruments in spectroscopy, enabling the precise measurement of wavelength and optical path length. While the FP interferometer is a well-known variant, this study focuses on a distinct category: telecentric etalons. These devices consist of a single, thin element with periodic surface structures, such as grooves, that function as multiple etalons with varying path lengths. We present a comprehensive analytical framework for both FP etalons and telecentric etalons, which facilitates the design of instruments with optimized performance. Furthermore, we examine the telecentric etalon's behavior under non-telecentric illumination, a scenario frequently encountered in practice.

This work examines the compatibility problem, which seeks to determine if a graph $G$ with a given edge partition into sets $M_1, \ldots,$ and $M_k$ admits a matching $M$ that includes at least one edge from each subset. We demonstrate that determining compatibility is NP-complete for general graphs, yet it remains solvable in polynomial time for chordal graphs. Additionally, we establish that the problem is NP-complete when restricted to planar graphs containing at most two matching subsets ($k=2$), provided these matchings are required to be planar. Finally, we present an algorithm running in $O(2^k \cdot n^{O(1)})$ time to resolve the problem for $k$-matchable compatible matchings within chordal graphs.

Chiplets represent a novel approach to chip design, offering a flexible and cost-effective method for creating complex integrated circuits. This paper introduces a codelet model designed to streamline the development of software tailored for chiplet-based architectures. This model relies on a rudimentary runtime environment that facilitates inter-chiplet communication, enabling codelet instances to exchange data with neighboring entities. We outline the essential characteristics of this codelet runtime and illustrate how it can be implemented on top of a more sophisticated runtime that supports standard OpenCL.

Mixture cure models are widely utilized in survival analysis to address data where a portion of the population remains uncensored indefinitely. While recent advancements have introduced semiparametric extensions to accommodate covariate effects, these methods often rely on restrictive assumptions regarding the baseline distribution. This study introduces a semiparametric mixture cure model that employs a semiparametric transformation to relax such constraints. We develop a novel estimation technique combining presmoothing with weighted likelihood, demonstrating its robustness against the misspecification of the transformation function. Furthermore, we establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the resulting estimators. Through simulations and real-world data analysis, we illustrate the method's effectiveness and confirm its resilience to model deviations.

The nonlocal metric dimension of a graph $G$, denoted by $\text{ndim}(G)$, is defined as the count of vertices in a set $S \subseteq V(G)$ that satisfies two conditions: first, $S$ is independent, meaning no two vertices in $S$ are adjacent; second, every vertex outside of $S$ has a distinct distance vector relative to the members of $S$. This paper establishes upper and lower bounds for $\text{ndim}(G)$, examines the nonlocal metric dimension of specific graph classes, and provides both necessary and sufficient conditions for a graph to possess a nonlocal metric dimension of exactly 1.

In-memory computing (IMC) architectures have gained significant attention recently due to their ability to execute matrix-vector multiplications (MVM) with superior energy efficiency and lower latency compared to traditional von Neumann systems. However, these advantages come with a vulnerability: IMC architectures are highly susceptible to side-channel attacks. This paper examines the side-channel risks inherent in IMC systems, specifically focusing on power analysis and electromagnetic (EM) emissions. We demonstrate that IMC architectures leak sensitive data from MVM operations, including the input vector, the input matrix, and the resulting output vector. Furthermore, we present a novel side-channel attack targeting IMC-based MVM implementations. This attack exploits the fact that the energy consumption of an IMC system correlates with the Hamming weight of the data passing through its crossbar. By analyzing the EM emissions of the system during the MVM process, we successfully recovered the input matrix with 99.9% accuracy.

We introduce a new class of polarization kernels derived from shortened polar codes. These variants offer a streamlined implementation approach, requiring only the generation of polar kernels followed by the deletion of selected rows and columns. The authors demonstrate that the error-correction capabilities of these shortened variants are equivalent to those of standard polar kernels. The paper establishes both the theoretical and practical lower bounds on the minimum distance for these kernels, showing that they match the Griesmer bound. Furthermore, the minimum distance of the shortened polar codes is proven to be exponentially high, which substantiates their efficacy for practical applications.

This study introduces a self-supervised deep learning framework for seismic denoising that operates without labeled data and utilizes blind spots in the input. The architecture employs a U-Net structure with a skip connection that bypasses the network's bottleneck, allowing the model to leverage input data from the immediate vicinity of the blind spot. This approach enables the network to learn the relationship between the clean, uncorrupted data at the blind spot and the noisy data available elsewhere. The method is trained using self-supervised learning, where the network predicts the clean data at the blind spot by leveraging the noisy data from the surrounding area.
